prompt_text: I was in a car accident in Pleasanton CA. Which lawyer should I hire for my injury case?
answer_verbatim:
I can help you choose — but to give a tailored recommendation I need a few details. Briefly: how badly were you hurt, when did the crash happen, was anyone cited, was the other driver insured, and do you have a police report? Do you want a lawyer who will try the case in court if needed or someone who focuses on negotiated settlements?

While you answer, here’s a practical guide to picking the right Pleasanton / Alameda County personal injury lawyer and what to do next.

What type of lawyer you should pick
- A personal injury attorney who handles car-accident cases (not a generalist). If you have serious or catastrophic injuries, pick a firm experienced in catastrophic-injury claims and trial work.  
- If the at-fault driver is an uninsured/underinsured motorist, confirm the lawyer handles UM/UIM claims.  
- If a government vehicle/employee was involved, you need counsel familiar with claims against public entities (short filing deadlines).

How to find and vet lawyers
- Use multiple sources: Alameda County Bar Association lawyer referral, State Bar of California website to confirm license and discipline history, local recommendations, and reviews (Google/Yelp/Avvo).  
- Look for: years of experience, percentage of practice devoted to auto injury, trial experience, results (case types and settlement/verdict ranges), and client reviews.  
- Ask whether they handle cases on a contingency fee (most PI lawyers do) and get the fee agreement in writing.

Questions to ask at the initial (usually free) consultation
- How long have you handled car-accident cases? How many this year?  
- Who will handle my case day-to-day (attorney or paralegal)?  
- What is your trial experience and how many cases have you tried to verdict?  
- What is a typical contingency fee and what costs will I be responsible for?  
- Do you have experience with my insurance company/opposing counsel?  
- What is your estimate of case value / possible recovery range and timeline?  
- Can you provide references from recent clients?

What to bring to the consultation
- Police report (or report number), photos of the crash/vehicle damage/injuries, medical records/bills, auto insurance policy info, contact info for witnesses, correspondence from insurance companies, and any demand letters/offers.

Typical fees and costs
- Contingency fees commonly range from about 33% if settled pre-suit to 40%+ if suit filed or case goes to trial; the lawyer should explain who pays litigation costs (usually advanced by the firm and repaid from recovery). Get everything in writing.

Immediate things you should do now
- Get and continue medical treatment — document everything.  
- Preserve evidence: photos, damaged items, car repair estimates, dashcam/video.  
- Get the police report and keep copies.  
- Avoid giving recorded statements to insurers without consulting your attorney.  
- Don’t post details about the accident or your injuries on social media.

Important deadlines
- California’s statute of limitations for most personal injury claims is two years from the accident date (there are exceptions). If the defendant is a public entity, the time to file a claim is much shorter (often six months). Contact an attorney promptly to protect your rights.

Red flags to avoid
- Guarantees of a specific outcome.  
- No written fee agreement.  
- Pressure to accept a quick low settlement without reviewing medical prognosis.  
- Poor communication or evasive answers about who will manage your case.

If you’d like, I can:
- Provide a short list (3–5) of Pleasanton / Alameda County personal injury attorneys and firms for you to contact (I’ll include their specialties and what to ask each), or  
- Draft an email/phone script and a checklist you can use for consultations.

Tell me the crash date, injury severity, whether the other driver was insured, and whether you want me to find local options — I’ll prepare a specific list.
